notes.title: Sourdough hydration
notes.content:
Hydration is water weight divided by flour weight. 70% is a good start: the dough is easy to shape and still gives an open crumb.

Higher hydration (75-80%) gives bigger holes but is sticky; use wet hands and a bench scraper.
Whole wheat flour drinks more water, so add 5% more when swapping in a third whole wheat.

notes.title: Sourdough hydration tips
notes.content:
Hydration means the weight of water compared with the weight of flour. Begin at 70%: easy to shape, and the crumb still opens up.

With 75-80% hydration you get larger holes, but the dough is sticky, so wet your hands and use a scraper.
Whole wheat absorbs more water: add about 5% extra when a third of the flour is whole wheat.

notes.title: Easy run pace
notes.content:
An easy run should feel conversational: you can speak full sentences. For me that is about 6:15 per km, or heart rate below 145.

notes.title: useDebounce hook
Restart a Kubernetes deployment
notes.content:
# Rolling restart without changing the image
kubectl rollout restart deployment/api -n production

# Watch it finish
kubectl rollout status deployment/api -n production

# Roll back if the new pods fail
kubectl rollout undo deployment/api -n production

notes.title: Kubernetes probes
notes.content:
Liveness probe: is the container still working? If it fails, kubelet restarts the container.
Readiness probe: should this pod get traffic? If it fails, the pod is removed from the service endpoints but not restarted.
Startup probe: gives slow-starting apps time before the liveness probe begins.

A liveness probe that checks a dependency (like the database) can cause restart storms. Keep it cheap and local.

notes.title: Debugging CrashLoopBackOff
notes.content:
A pod in CrashLoopBackOff starts, crashes, and is restarted with growing delays.

1. kubectl describe pod: read Events and the last state's exit code.
2. kubectl logs --previous: the logs of the crashed container.
3. Exit code 137 usually means out of memory; check the memory limit.
4. A failing liveness probe also causes restarts: see [[Kubernetes probes]].

notes.title: Platform runbook
notes.content:
Before a release: check the pod memory limits and plan the [[Rolling deployments]].
If pods restart after the release, start with [[Debugging CrashLoopBackOff]] and the [[Kubernetes probes]] note.
Rollback command is in the Kubernetes snippets.

notes.title: Q3 Product Roadmap
notes.content:
Q3 Product Roadmap

Goals: reduce time-to-first-note below 30 seconds, ship search by meaning to all users, and keep the free plan within its limits.

July: onboarding checklist and import from Markdown files.
August: Ask with citations, tag and folder suggestions.
September: graph view, duplicate detection and the mobile drawer.

Risks: the free server sleeps after 15 idle minutes, so the first request is slow. Mitigation: show a waking-up notice and keep the page responsive.

Success metrics: 70% of new accounts create 5 notes in their first week; median search takes under 1.5 seconds once the server is awake.
keyPoints: The goals are time-to-first-note under 30 seconds, search by meaning for everyone, and staying within the free plan.
July brings onboarding and Markdown import, August brings Ask with citations, September brings the graph and duplicate detection.
The main risk is the free server sleeping after 15 idle minutes, handled with a waking-up notice.

notes.title: Embeddings and RAG study notes
notes.content:
# Embeddings and retrieval-augmented generation

An embedding turns text into a list of numbers so that texts with similar meaning end up close together. Cosine similarity measures how close.

Semantic search embeds the query and returns the notes whose vectors are nearest. It finds 'stop pods restarting' even if the note only says 'CrashLoopBackOff'.

Retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) first retrieves the most relevant passages, then asks a model to answer using only those passages and to cite them.

Chunking: long documents are split into overlapping chunks of a few hundred words, so a question can match the right paragraph instead of a whole file.

Common failure: answering from general knowledge when the notes do not contain the answer. Fix: tell the model to say 'not found' when the passages do not support an answer.
keyPoints: An embedding turns text into numbers so texts with similar meaning are close, and cosine similarity measures how close.
RAG retrieves the most relevant passages first, then answers only from them and cites them.
To avoid answering from general knowledge, the model must say 'not found' when the passages do not support an answer.
